title: A repair table with a waiting list
paragraphs: Our neighbourhood has held a repair afternoon once a month since March. Residents bring small items to a table in the community hall, where volunteers help them decide what can be repaired. I joined the group last Saturday with a lamp that had stopped working. I expected to leave it with an expert and collect it later. Instead, a volunteer asked me to sit beside her while she checked it.

The lamp was not repaired immediately. Its cable was damaged, and a suitable replacement had to be ordered. The volunteer explained what she had checked and wrote the part number on a card. She did not promise that the lamp would work after the cable was replaced. Another problem might appear when the first one was fixed. I appreciated the careful explanation, even though it meant another visit.

While we waited, I spoke to a woman who had brought a jacket. Before coming to the hall, she had watched a video about replacing a zip. She still could not work out where to begin. A volunteer helped her practise on a piece of spare cloth before touching the jacket. The task took longer than she had expected, but she said that she now understood the first step.

By lunchtime, people were waiting outside. The organisers had prepared ten appointment cards, but more than twenty residents had arrived. They asked visitors whether they could return in the afternoon. Some could; others had already arranged transport home. We realised that a fair waiting system would need more thought than simply giving everyone a number.

I have not collected my lamp yet, so I cannot call the visit a complete success. However, I have learned how to describe its problem and what to ask next time. The group has now added a booking option, while keeping a few places for people who cannot book online. The repair table is useful not just because things may work again. It also gives people a chance to understand a task that once seemed impossible.
translation: 从三月起，我们社区每月举行一次维修下午活动。居民把小物件带到社区大厅，志愿者帮助判断哪些可以修理。上周六，我带着一盏坏了的灯加入活动。我以为交给专家，稍后取回即可，但一位志愿者请我坐在旁边，看她检查。
灯没有当场修好。电线已损坏，需要订购合适的替换件。志愿者解释了检查内容，把零件编号写在卡片上。她没有保证换线后灯一定能工作，因为修复第一个问题后，可能还会发现别的问题。虽然要再跑一趟，我仍感谢这番谨慎解释。
等待时，我和一位带夹克来的女士聊天。来大厅之前，她看过更换拉链的视频，却仍不知从何下手。志愿者先帮她在一块备用布料上练习，然后才处理夹克。任务比预期耗时，但她说自己终于理解了第一步。
午餐时，人们已在外面排队。组织者准备了十张预约卡，却来了二十多位居民。他们问访客能否下午再来，有些人可以，有些人已安排了回家的交通。我们意识到，公平的等待安排不能只靠给每个人一个号码。
我还没取回灯，因此不能说这次活动完全成功。不过，我已学会描述问题，也知道下次该问什么。团队现在增加了预约选项，同时为无法网上预约的人保留几个名额。维修桌的价值不仅在于东西可能恢复功能，也在于帮助人们理解曾经看似不可能的任务。

questions.prompt: What does the narrator learn from the repair afternoon?
options: Getting an item repaired can also involve understanding the work and its limits.
Every visitor can expect a complete repair during the first visit.
Volunteers should always do the work without explaining it.
questions.explanation: 活动既帮助处理物件，也让居民了解步骤、风险和需要继续确认的事情。

questions.prompt: Why does the lamp need another visit?
options: The narrator left the lamp at home.
The volunteer refused to examine electrical items.
A replacement cable has to be obtained, and further checks may still be needed.
questions.explanation: 第二段说明要订电线，并且换线后也未必解决所有问题。

questions.prompt: Why practise on spare cloth before working on the jacket?
options: It avoids the need to replace the zip at all.
It allows the visitor to try a step without immediately risking the jacket.
It proves that watching videos is always useless.
questions.explanation: 练习布提供了尝试步骤的机会；文章并没有否定所有视频教学。

questions.prompt: Why is “had watched” used in the jacket paragraph?
options: Watching the video happened before the woman came to the hall.
Watching the video is an unfinished habit in the present.
The video will be watched after the repair.
questions.explanation: 过去完成时把看视频放在过去来到大厅之前。

questions.prompt: Why mention places for people who cannot book online?
options: To show that the organisers plan to stop taking bookings.
To claim that everyone has the same access to online tools.
To show that improving the queue should consider different visitors’ needs.
questions.explanation: 预约便利之外，也需要给无法在线操作的人留入口。

notes: 原创学习文章，人物、团队与活动为虚构情境，不是新闻报道或研究结论。
等级为教学分级参考；语法解释与阅读理解采用文内证据，开放讨论允许不同有依据的判断。
